name: Features Grid — Driftboard
html:
Design without the busywork

Three habits that keep a team's files trustworthy, whether it is two people or two hundred touching the same project.

  • Always in sync

    Every edit saves the instant it happens, so nobody opens a file wondering if it is the latest version.

    Comments pin to the exact layer they describe, so nothing gets lost between a screenshot and a chat thread.

name: Feature Grid — Formloom
html:
Everything a site needs, one canvas

Design, content, motion, and commerce used to mean four different tools. Formloom keeps them in one place, so nothing gets lost between handoffs.

  • Visual designer

    Full control over structure, spacing, and style without leaving the canvas or waiting on a stylesheet change.

  • Content engine

    Model any content type once, then let editors update copy and images without ever touching layout.

  • Motion and interactions

    Layer scroll, hover, and click-triggered animation onto any element — no plugin, no exported keyframes.

  • Commerce

    Sell products, subscriptions, and digital downloads straight from the same canvas you designed in.

  • Global hosting

    Every publish goes out over a fast edge network, with automatic backups behind every change.

  • Built-in SEO

    Clean semantic markup and editable metadata ship on every page — no separate technical audit needed.

name: Split Feature — Formloom
html:
Describe the page. Watch it take shape.

Staring at a blank canvas is the slowest part of any build. Tell Formloom's assistant what the page needs to do, and it drafts a full structure — sections, copy slots, and imagery — ready to refine.

Nothing is locked in a black box. Every section it drafts is an ordinary layer you can restyle, reorder, or delete, exactly the way you would with anything you built by hand.

Step 1

Import and link repeated text (with Stringly's suggestions)

Bring the text you care about into Stringly, then identify the copy you're reusing in multiple places and link it together. Now, whenever you make an edit once, it syncs to every instance.

Step 2

Publish approved text to your reusable library

Identify the copy you want to standardize and reuse, and publish it to your library. Now anyone on your team can find approved language in seconds.

Step 3

Share your library across teams

Skip the digging around and pull approved copy straight into designs from Stringly's plugin. Drag and drop copy from the Assets tab so the right text gets used from the start.
